question: Did the risk of a motorist being killed per mile driven in NYC decline from 2013 to 2025? Make a chart and answer based on this crash data.

options.metric: Sum of number_of_motorist_killed by calendar year of crash_date (reported motorist deaths).
options.denominator: None; an annual count, not a rate.
options.reason: An annual fatality count directly describes the reported motorist-death burden without implying an exposure denominator that is not in the file.
options.answer: This crash file cannot establish whether motorist-death risk per mile declined; it records 110 motorist deaths in 2013 and 81 in 2025, with yearly counts varying in between.
options.interpretation: This partly answers the question by showing the annual sum of reported motorist deaths among NYC police-reported crashes with an assignable date in calendar years 2013-2025: the count is 110 in 2013 and 81 in 2025. An annual count is a defensible description of reported fatality burden, but it is not adjusted for travel exposure. The file has no miles-driven or vehicle-miles-traveled denominator, so it leaves unanswered whether the per-mile risk declined. The check found 0 missing motorist-death counts among 2,132,218 in-range crashes, so none were excluded for that reason; observed date endpoints span Jan 1-Dec 31 in every year but do not prove day-by-day completeness, and records without an assignable crash year are outside the plan's year filter.

options.metric: 1,000 times the sum of number_of_motorist_killed divided by the count of eligible crash records, by calendar year of crash_date.
options.denominator: Count of NYC police-reported crashes in the year with a non-NULL number_of_motorist_killed value, scaled to 1,000 records.
options.reason: Scaling reported motorist deaths by crash-record volume offers an interpretable within-dataset comparison when an exposure-based per-mile rate is unavailable.
options.answer: This crash file cannot establish whether motorist-death risk per mile declined; the proxy measure is 0.54 reported motorist deaths per 1,000 crash records in 2013 and 0.95 in 2025.
options.interpretation: This partly answers the question with reported motorist deaths per 1,000 NYC police-reported crash records that have a known death count, grouped by calendar year of crash_date from 2013 through 2025; the plotted measure is 0.54 in 2013 and 0.95 in 2025. This crash-record-normalized measure describes reported deaths relative to reported crash volume, but it is not exposure-adjusted per mile. Because miles driven are absent, it leaves unanswered whether the risk per mile declined. The check found 0 missing outcome counts among 2,132,218 in-range crashes, so all were retained; records without an assignable crash year fall outside the plan, and observed date endpoints span each year without proving daily completeness; the denominator fell by 98,568 rows from 211,486 in 2019 to 112,918 in 2020, so across those years a rise or fall in this measure can come from this denominator change and not the outcome, and the comparison requires caution.

answer:
The crash data cannot establish whether motorist-death risk per mile declined; reported motorist deaths numbered 110 in 2013 and 81 in 2025, with annual counts varying in between ([bar chart](out/option_1.png)).
The crash data cannot establish the per-mile trend; reported motorist deaths per 1,000 crash records were 0.54 in 2013 and 0.95 in 2025 ([line chart](out/option_2.png)).
